figure: Figure 8.1 — Where inference computation and data movement actually live
issue: The prominent red gradient arrow on the right spans all three color groups (compute/blue, memory/orange, interconnect/green) with the label 'capacity grows, speed drops, distance grows,' but the caption explicitly states 'only the memory hierarchy is a smallest-to-largest ladder.' The arrow's label applies cleanly only to the orange memory levels: 'capacity grows' does not describe tensor cores or interconnect links; 'speed drops' conflates compute throughput with memory access latency when crossing the blue tensor-cores box. The visual encoding of a single monotone gradient across all three groups works against the book's central claim that compute, memory bandwidth/capacity, and interconnect are distinct constraint types. The caption corrects the misreading after the fact, but the figure's first-impression signal is wrong.
evidence: Arrow spans from the 'registers' box (top) to the 'other GPUs / remote' box (bottom), crossing the blue 'tensor cores / ALU' box. Caption: 'the colors mark the groups, and only the memory hierarchy is a smallest-to-largest ladder.' Bottom note: 'the gradient makes compute, bandwidth, capacity and interconnect distinct constraints' — yet the arrow visually unifies them into one gradient.
acceptance_test: Restrict the red arrow to span only the orange (memory) boxes — registers through HBM — with a visual break or gap where it would cross the blue tensor-cores box. Alternatively, add a short inline annotation near the arrow such as '(memory hierarchy)' to scope the gradient. Re-render and confirm the arrow no longer visually implies that tensor cores and interconnect links are levels of the same capacity/speed ladder.

figure: Figure 7.6 — Inference vs fine-tuning memory floor
issue: The QLoRA footnote annotation states 'KV 24 GB' but Figures 7.7 (PDF 149) and 7.8 (PDF 151) both use '24.9 GB' for the same 9.5K-context FP16 KV on the same 70B full-MHA model. If the QLoRA scenario uses the same 9.5K max context as the inference bar (which yields ~165 GB = 140 + 24.9), the KV should be ~24.9 GB, not 24 GB. With KV = 24.9, the QLoRA total would be 35 + 24.9 + 1 = 60.9 ≈ 61 GB, not the printed ~60 GB. The 1 GB discrepancy suggests either (a) 24.9 was incorrectly rounded down to 24, or (b) the QLoRA scenario silently uses the 9.2K canonical context (9,200 × 2.62 MB ≈ 24.1 GB) while the inference bar uses 9.5K — but the figure does not state different context lengths per scenario.
evidence: Figure 7.6 footnote: 'QLoRA: 4-bit (NF4) base 35 GB + KV 24 GB + LoRA adapters/optimizer ~1 GB.' Bar label: '~60 GB.' 35 + 24 + 1 = 60 (internally consistent with 24). Figure 7.7 caption: '24.9 GB/request max-FP16 KV (9.5K max context).' Figure 7.8: 'KV 24.9 GB' at 9.5K. Inference bar in 7.6: ~165 GB = 140 + 24.9 (implies 9.5K).
acceptance_test: Decide whether all three scenarios in Figure 7.6 use the same context length. If 9.5K: change QLoRA KV to '24.9 GB' and total to '~61 GB' (or '~60–61 GB'). If 9.2K: add an explicit context annotation to the QLoRA footnote (e.g., 'KV ~24 GB at 9.2K canonical'). Confirm the bar height and label are updated to match. Verify no downstream text references '~60 GB' for QLoRA that would also need updating.

issue: The figure title reads 'Whole-clip denoising: Wan2.2 TI2V-5B' and the caption reads 'Wan2.2 TI2V-5B whole-clip denoising,' but the main processing box inside the figure reads 'Wan2.2 dense TI2V-5B + scheduler.' The qualifier 'dense' (distinguishing from MoE variants) appears only in the inner box, not in the title or caption. This is a naming inconsistency within a single figure.
evidence: Title: 'Whole-clip denoising: Wan2.2 TI2V-5B.' Main box: 'Wan2.2 dense TI2V-5B + scheduler.' Caption: 'Wan2.2 TI2V-5B whole-clip denoising.'
acceptance_test: Add 'dense' to the figure title and/or caption so all three locations read 'Wan2.2 dense TI2V-5B,' or remove 'dense' from the inner box if the distinction is not needed. Confirm consistency across title, box label, and caption after the edit.

issue: The caption states 'the faint vertical rules inside the KV band mark those 24.9 GB request slots,' but at 150 dpi the vertical rules within the orange dotted KV band are barely discernible against the dot-pattern fill. If the rules cannot be reliably counted at print size, the caption's reference to them is misleading — the reader is told to look for a visual element they may not be able to see. The rules serve a pedagogical purpose (showing how many request slots fit), so they need to be visible enough to count.
evidence: Caption: 'the faint vertical rules inside the KV band mark those 24.9 GB request slots.' Visual inspection at 150 dpi: vertical lines are present but very low contrast against the orange dot-pattern background; counting them is difficult.
acceptance_test: Increase the contrast or weight of the vertical rules (e.g., solid thin white or dark lines instead of faint lines on a patterned background), or change the KV band fill to a solid color so the rules stand out. Re-render at 150 dpi and confirm the rules are countable. If the rules remain intentionally subtle, remove the caption's reference to them and instead state the slot count in prose.
